heartbeat.title: Warmth beats a cold restatement
heartbeat.body_html: The clearest lesson from this month's winners is that matching the tone of the inbox unit to the emotional reality of the message keeps paying off. Personalizing the subscription cancellation with a first name and a warm appeal won, and leading the welcome inbox with a real customer quote won on revenue per recipient. Across abandon cart and browse, the same pattern held: subject and preview lines that feel human and specific pull people in more reliably than generic offer restatements. We keep testing this deliberately so the flows get sharper every month, not just when something breaks.

narrative.html: Flow revenue rose 30.3% to 13,122 USD, with revenue per email delivered climbing from 0.247 to 0.302 USD. The flows we manage did more work per send this month, not just more sending.
Flows earned 13.7x more per email than campaigns (0.302 USD vs 0.022 USD) and drove 55% of all email revenue. The automated layer continues to be the most efficient email you run.

Flow share of total store revenue held at 6.0% on 218,007 USD in store sales, right in line with the 12-month range. Deliverability stayed clean, with unsubscribes at 0.297% and spam complaints at 0.007%.

Campaigns landed at 0.022 USD per email across 14 sends. Campaigns are your in-house program, so this is just an observation, but if it would ever help to have a second set of eyes on subject lines or cadence, we're happy to take a look.

monthly.title_sub: Flows delivered 13,122 USD in August, up 30.3% on the prior month, and earned 13.7x more per email than campaigns.

heartbeat.title: Specific beats abstract in the subject line
heartbeat.body_html: Two of this month's four winners came from the same idea: replacing vague framing with something concrete. In Bounce Back, naming the subscriber's actual last flavor and first name beat the generic "your bag" control, and a product-state hook ("Your bag isn't going to refill itself") outperformed a softer observation line. The transferable lesson is that the more precisely an email speaks to what a person did or owns, the harder it works. We are now rolling that specificity principle across other flows, which is exactly the kind of compounding refinement the testing program is built to find.

narrative.html: Flows earned $10,068 in July, down 7.7% from last month, with revenue per email delivered easing from $0.268 to $0.247. Flow share of total store revenue came in at 5.1%, the softest reading in the 12-month series, tracking a quieter month across the store overall. We are watching this closely and the testing pipeline below is aimed squarely at rebuilding per-email yield.

Flows earned 8.8x more per email than campaigns this month, $0.247 against $0.028. Even in a slower month, the automated flows continue to do the heavy lifting, contributing 38% of all email revenue from a fraction of the send volume.

Campaigns sent 17 broadcasts in-house at $0.028 per email delivered. That is your team's turf and you know your calendar best, but if it would ever help to have a second set of eyes on campaign structure or segmentation, we are glad to take a look at no cost.

Deliverability stayed clean, with unsubscribes at 0.327% of delivered and spam complaints at just 0.01%. Healthy list hygiene keeps the flows landing in the inbox, which protects every dollar the automations earn.

monthly.title_sub: Flows brought in $10,068 in July, holding a 5.1% share of total store revenue while earning 8.8x more per email than campaigns.
